resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline's real name is Gamasa–Finosa/Fenosa (خط غاز جمصة – فينوسا); 'Veunsa' is a garbled transliteration of فينوسا. Egyptian Presidency national-projects page describes the line as built/added in 2015 to supply the West Damietta power plant; youm7 reports construction completed Nov 2015 and the plant being fed gas. Both establish operating status. Note: the original current_ref petro-news.com/95212 (flagged DEAD_LINK in the brief) is in fact live again (verified 200, mentions the جمصة-فينوسا line among Egypt's implemented gas projects) and could stay as a supporting cite.
StartYear1=2015 corroborated by two independent sources: Presidency page says the Gamasa–Finosa line was 'added during 2015'; youm7 reports construction completed November 2015. Consistent.

VALUE CONTRADICTION — UNIT MISMATCH. youm7 (and the pipeline's popular name) give the design flow as 6.8 million CUBIC METRES per day (6.8 مليون متر مكعب يوميا), i.e. ~6.8 MMcm/d ≈ 240 MMcf/d. GEM records Capacity=6.80 in MMcf/d, which mistakes cubic metres for cubic feet and understates the flow by ~35x. The '6.8' figure is supported by a single strong source; recommend Update either correct CapacityUnits to MMcm/d or convert to ~240 MMcf/d. No independent second source states a capacity figure.

Both sources place the line in Damietta governorate, Egypt: it runs from chamber No.10 on the Idku–Damietta 32-inch line at Gamasa (جمصة, Damietta gov.) to the Finosa/West Damietta power-plant intake. Supports StartState/Province=Damietta, Start/End CountryOrArea=Egypt (34 km, 42-inch per both sources).

VALUE CONTRADICTION. Three independent sources (Presidency, youm7, petro-news) all state the cost as ~397 million EGP (~US$50.4M); youm7 gives 'approximately 397 million pounds'. GEM records SegmentCost=340,000,000 EGP, which no source supports. Refs added but recommend Update revise SegmentCost to 397,000,000 EGP (or flag the delta).

ATTRIBUTION NUANCE. Sources name GASCO (الشركة المصرية للغازات الطبيعية / جاسكو) as the company that built and operates the line (design/execution by Petrojet). GASCO is the wholly-owned gas-transmission subsidiary of EGAS (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co), so GEM's Owner1=EGAS 100% is defensible at the holding level, but the direct operator/builder is GASCO — consider recording GASCO as operator. No source contradicts EGAS ownership.
